whatThisIs: A statement of where the round-1 entry stands with the lockout still ahead, and of every outside claim gathered about it during the day. It exists so that after the football there is a dated record of what was known BEFORE, rather than a reconstruction assembled afterwards.
whatThisIsNot: NOT part of the entry, and NOT a second entry. It records no pick, changes no pick, and the grader reads round-01.json alone.
NOT a revision. Nothing in the four outside sources captured today altered a single selection, and the verification below is the proof rather than the assurance.

entryIntegrity.claim: The entry has been recorded once and never touched since.
entryIntegrity.whyThisIsTheImportantPart: A track record is only worth keeping if the picks provably predate the results. One commit, thirteen minutes after the picks were generated, and a byte-identical file thirty-three hours later is a stronger statement than any promise in a README. Anyone can re-run: git log -- efl/data/rounds/round-01.json

theEntry.noteOnThat: Seven from seven at home was flagged when the entry was recorded, before anyone knew whether it would look clever. Home advantage is in the club rating so a tilt is expected; seven of seven is a strong one and remains the single most likely explanation of any result in either direction.

perPick.for: Named 'the meta' by ScottyFEFL (4 Aug) and ranked number-one midfielder by NatetheGreat (14 Aug), who cites 7.8 points per round and 357 points last season, 22 goals and assists in League One and 123 interceptions plus key passes.
perPick.against: His opponent Luton is O'Haire's most-trusted League One promotion selection — unbeaten final eleven, 2.45 xG per game, third-best shot ratio, and only two sides allowed fewer shots. NatetheGreat's 'do not put be off with the fixture' was a warning we initially filed as an aside.
perPick.ownership: 28.3% reported. Widely tipped, moderately owned — and this project wrongly called him a 'consensus pick' this morning before that number was known.

perPick.for: Oldham are an O'Haire promotion selection at 4/1, with 110 big chances created against 82 conceded and a manager with six promotions. Round-1 opponent Port Vale scored 36 goals from almost 50 xG last season.
perPick.against: The same paragraph: 'their defensive record probably flatters them — only 44 conceded from around 58 xGA.' Fourteen goals of defensive over-performance is exactly what regresses, and a goalkeeper pick is a bet on clean sheets.

perPick.for: An O'Haire Top Goalscorer selection at 33/1 on a fit argument — Bradford were the second-lowest scorers in last season's top half despite finishing fourth, producing crossing volume with no natural centre-forward. His opponent Peterborough is a relegation selection with the second-most shots conceded in League One. NatetheGreat separately picks Bradford at home to Peterborough as a team.
Cambridge's promotion is credited to 'only 8.1 opposition shots per game alongside a 0.59 shot ratio and 0.66 big-chance ratio' — a defensive case, and we own the defender.
perPick.against: Nothing directly. Both other sources that like Cambridge take its forward, Ben Knight, instead.

perPick.for: Grimsby 'created more big chances than anybody' with one of League Two's strongest shot and big-chance ratios, and are named a chief danger to the favourite.

perPick.note: Neither Bristol City nor Stoke is discussed in any of the four sources. That is silence, not endorsement and not criticism — these documents cover the clubs their authors have opinions about.

perPick.against: THREE independent sources. O'Haire makes Blackburn a recommended relegation selection at 11/2, on 42 goals from 55.4 xG — 'the biggest attacking underperformance in the Championship' — plus a 20th-place finish, O'Neill's departure and 'precious little summer strengthening'. NatetheGreat picks Wolves at home to Blackburn at a reported 46.4% and says Blackburn 'look set for a rough season'. His number-one defender is a Wolves player in that same fixture.
perPick.ourSide: 0.5% owned on the official feed, against a reported 46.4% on the other side of the same match.

perPick.note: Reading is not mentioned once in O'Haire's League One preview. Absence proves nothing and no inference is drawn from it.

whatTonightAndTomorrowSettle: Wolves v Blackburn is the only outright disagreement in the set: we hold one side of a match and a well-backed outside pick holds the other. Ninety minutes decides it with nothing left to interpret.
Lewis Wing's return grades two claims at once — the community's 'best all-round asset in this game' and our own decision to captain him into the division's best-trending opponent.
Whether seven home picks was a model finding a real edge or a tilt nobody had checked.

Individually gradeable outside claims, none of which is a squad and none of which will be scored as one: twelve tipster players and three team tips, three defenders, three midfielders, three forwards, six named differentials and six team picks.
predictionsDeliberatelyNotMade: No score, no points total and no expected finish is recorded here. The model produced a ranking, not a forecast of returns, and inventing a number now to be graded against later would be inventing the standard as well as the result.
